title: GRID: Modeling Health Influencer Discourse as Argument Networks for Credibility Assessment
abstract: arXiv:2610.27149v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Health-related discussions on social media are increasingly shaped by influencers who offer diverse, and often competing perspectives on the same issue. Yet, such content is typically evaluated in isolation, without considering the broader discourse in which it appears. We introduce GRID (Grounded Reasoning over Interconnected Discourse), a framework for evaluating influencer content through collective inference over the surrounding discourse. GRID represents each video as an argumentation graph connecting claims to its central message, or takeaway, links related claims and takeaways across videos, grounds claims in scientific evidence, and jointly infers credibility over the resulting network. We evaluate GRID on an end-to-end health-related content validation task using 569 influencer videos grounded in expert assessments. translated_title: GRID：将健康类网红话语建模为论辩网络以进行可信度评估
translated_abstract: 社交媒体上与健康相关的讨论日益受到网红的影响，这些网红对同一问题提供多样且常常相互竞争的观点。然而，此类内容通常被孤立地评估，而没有考虑其所处的更广泛的话语背景。我们提出了GRID（Grounded Reasoning over Interconnected Discourse，互联话语上的有据推理），这是一个通过对周围话语进行集体推理来评估网红内容的框架。GRID将每个视频表示为一个论辩图，将各论点连接到其中心信息（即要点），在视频之间关联相关的论点和要点，将论点与科学证据相印证，并在由此形成的网络上联合推断可信度。我们在一个端到端的健康相关内容验证任务上对GRID进行了评估，该任务使用569个基于专家评估的网红视频。结果表明，考虑更广泛的话语背景能够改进网红内容的验证效果。
tldr: 提出GRID框架，将健康类网红视频建模为相互关联的论辩网络，结合科学证据进行联合可信度推断，证明考虑更广泛的话语背景能显著提升健康内容验证的效果。
